theory.intro: A **standard normal table** lists $P(Z<c)$, the area under the curve to the **left** of a positive $z$-score $c$. Every other region is built from those values using the complement, a subtraction, or the symmetry of the curve.
facts: The table gives $P(Z<c)$, the area to the left of $c$, and only for positive values of $c$.
$P(Z>c) = 1 - P(Z<c)$, because the two areas together make up the whole area of $1$.
$P(a<Z<b) = P(Z<b) - P(Z<a)$, so a middle strip is a difference of two left-hand areas.
For a score $x$, first find $z = \dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$, then use the table.
An **expected frequency** is $f = np$: the number of items $n$ times the probability $p$, rounded to a whole number.
steps: Convert the score to a $z$-score using $z = \dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$
Shade the required region under the curve
Read $P(Z<c)$ from the table and adjust it to the region wanted
Multiply the probability by $n$ for an expected frequency

development.question_text:
The masses of watermelons are normally distributed with a mean of $4.5$ kg and a standard deviation of $0.8$ kg.
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z & 0.75 & 1.50 & 2.25 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.7734 & 0.9332 & 0.9878 \\ \hline\end{array}$
Find the probability that a randomly chosen watermelon has a mass less than $5.7$ kg.

The number of daily visitors to a museum is normally distributed with a mean of $480$ and a standard deviation of $75$.
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z & 0.60 & 1.20 & 1.80 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.7257 & 0.8849 & 0.9641 \\ \hline\end{array}$
Find the probability that on a randomly chosen day there are more than $570$ visitors.

The daily takings of a café are normally distributed with a mean of $\$1450$ and a standard deviation of $\$180$.
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z & 0.50 & 1.00 & 1.50 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.6915 & 0.8413 & 0.9332 \\ \hline\end{array}$
Find the probability that a day's takings are less than $\$1270$.

The lengths of a species of fish are normally distributed with a mean of $28.0$ cm and a standard deviation of $2.5$ cm.
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline z & 0.60 & 1.60 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.7257 & 0.9452 \\ \hline\end{array}$
Find the probability that a randomly chosen fish is between $26.5$ cm and $32.0$ cm long.

A batch of $500$ light globes has lifetimes that are normally distributed with a mean of $1100$ hours and a standard deviation of $90$ hours.
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z & 0.80 & 1.60 & 2.40 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.7881 & 0.9452 & 0.9918 \\ \hline\end{array}$
How many globes are expected to last more than $1244$ hours?

How many saplings are expected to be between $70$ cm and $82$ cm tall?

mastery.question_text:
A machine fills bottles with volumes that are normally distributed with a mean of $375$ mL and a standard deviation of $6$ mL.
A bottle is rejected if it holds less than $366$ mL or more than $387$ mL.
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline z & 1.50 & 2.00 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.9332 & 0.9772 \\ \hline\end{array}$
In a production run of $4000$ bottles, how many are expected to be rejected?

The marks in an examination are normally distributed with a mean of $62$ and a standard deviation of $14$.
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline z & 1.26 & 1.27 & 1.28 & 1.29 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.8962 & 0.8980 & 0.8997 & 0.9015 \\ \hline\end{array}$
Using the table, find the approximate minimum mark a candidate needs in order to be in the top $10\%$.

How many workers are expected to travel between $12.8$ km and $24.5$ km?
